| M3 | Annual MAPP review | Monitoring, audit and review |
| M4 | Competence assurance for all safety-critical roles | Organisation and personnel — competence matrix (Element 2) |
| M5 | Contractor control | Organisation and personnel — contractor management |

# Element 5 — ALARP Demonstration (Framing)

*This element frames and records the demonstration. Every figure below is recorded from the external QRA by Process Risk Consultancy (role), February 2026. Nothing in this element has been computed by this assembly.*

**5.1 Recorded risk results (external QRA, February 2026):**

| Measure of risk | Recorded result | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Individual risk at the fence line | 3 × 10⁻⁶ per year | External QRA, Process Risk Consultancy (role), February 2026 |
| Societal risk | Within the tolerable-if-ALARP region | External QRA, Process Risk Consultancy (role), February 2026 |

Because the recorded societal-risk position is *tolerable-if-ALARP*, the demonstration turns on the adequacy of the risk-reduction measures below and the justification for measures rejected.

**5.2 Risk-reduction measures in place — hierarchy-of-controls ranking (KB-SNIP-HOC applied):**

| Rank | HoC level | Measure (duty-holder supplied) | Scenario(s) addressed | Character |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Engineering — passive | Mounding of the LPG bullets | S1 (removes fire-impingement BLEVE pathway for the bullets) | Prevention, passive — highest-order measure in place; no reliance on activation |
| 2 | Engineering — instrumented prevention | Overfill protection to API 2350 (duty-holder-cited standard) | S4 | Prevention |
| 3 | Engineering — active isolation | Transfer-line excess-flow valves | S2 (limits inventory loss on line failure) | Prevention / limitation |
| 4 | Engineering — active mitigation | Water deluge on the sphere | S1 (protects against fire impingement escalation) | Mitigation, active — requires actuation and water supply |
| 5 | Engineering — active mitigation | Rim-seal foam pourers | S3 | Mitigation, active |
| 6 | Administrative | Permit-to-work, MoC, operating-procedure suite, competence matrix (Element 2) | All | Supporting layer — not credited as primary risk reduction |

No scenario relies on administrative controls or PPE as its primary risk-reduction measure; each of S1–S4 carries at least one engineered measure. The residual reliance on **active** mitigation for S1 (deluge) and S3 (foam pourers) should be addressed in the demonstration narrative: state the availability/reliability basis for each active system, sourced from the external QRA or the duty-holder's maintenance regime → [GAP — availability and test-interval data for the deluge and foam-pourer systems not supplied].

**5.3 Measures considered and rejected.** A **gross-disproportion argument is recorded** for rejecting full relocation of the LPG sphere. [GAP — the supporting cost-benefit analysis (sacrifice vs risk-reduction quantification) behind the gross-disproportion argument was not supplied; the argument's substance must be appended by the duty-holder for the demonstration to stand at submission.]

**5.4 Framing note for the competent authority.** ALARP is demonstrated by argument, not by the risk numbers alone: the demonstration should walk each scenario from its PHA identification (Element 4) through the measures in place (5.2), the measures rejected with justification (5.3), and the recorded residual-risk position (5.1). The gaps flagged in 5.2–5.3 are the open items standing between this framing and a submission-ready demonstration.

# Element 6 — Internal Emergency Plan

*Recorded from duty-holder content.*

**6.1 Command structure.** A **site incident controller (role)** and a **deputy (role)** are designated **per shift**. The **Emergency Coordinator (role)** holds the emergency-response accountability; the **Site Manager (role)** is the site accountable person.

**6.2 Alarm, muster, and response arrangements:**

| Plan element | Arrangement (duty-holder supplied) | Risk-reduction measure (HoC-ranked per KB-SNIP-HOC) |
|---|---|---|
| Alerting | Two-tone site alarm | Administrative (alerting) — supported by automatic isolation on detection (engineering) |
| Muster | Designated assembly areas at the north and south gates | Engineered separation of muster points from the storage areas + automatic isolation on detection |
| Fixed-system activation | Foam and water-deluge activation from the control room | Active engineered mitigation, remotely operable (removes the need for local manual intervention at the fire scene) |
| External response | Liaison arrangements with the fire and rescue service pre-agreed | Administrative — pre-planned interface |
| Exercising | Annual joint exercise with the fire and rescue service; last held **May 2026**. Site emergency-preparedness testing twice yearly (Element 2.6) | Administrative — assurance of the above |

**6.3 Muster adequacy against the scenario set.** Muster points sit at the north and south gates. Scenario S1 (sphere BLEVE) and S2 (VCE) have off-site-reach potential per the PHA; [GAP — confirmation that the north- and south-gate muster locations sit outside the modelled consequence contours for S1–S3 was not supplied and depends on the per-scenario QRA outputs flagged in Element 4].

**6.4 Environmental emergency response.** Scenario S4 discharges to the interceptor with the river and water-supply intake 400 m east as receptors. [GAP — the plan's environmental-containment actions for S4 (interceptor isolation, boom deployment, water-company notification trigger) were not supplied.]

**6.5 Off-site interface.** The internal plan feeds the competent authority's external emergency-planning duty. [GAP — the information supplied to the external emergency-planning authority, and the date it was last provided, were not recorded in the notes.]

## Limitations

This document is **decision-support only** and was produced by an **assistive** tool: it structures the COMAH / Seveso III Safety Report argument and records the duty-holder's supplied content. The scenario identification is the site PHA's; every quantitative risk figure is recorded from the external QRA by Process Risk Consultancy (role) (February 2026) and none was computed or derived here; unsupplied elements are recorded as [GAP], never invented. It is not legal advice and does not constitute the Safety Report itself. **A competent person must review this output** — and the duty-holder's competent author must complete, own, and sign the Safety Report — before any reliance on it or submission to the competent authority.
